name: Leonard Smithers
bio: Publisher, bookseller and pornographer, who issued The Ballad of Reading Gaol and both of Wilde's last plays in book form when no respectable house would touch his name. One hundred and eight of Wilde's letters to him survive - more than to anyone else in this volume except Douglas and Ross - and they are overwhelmingly about proofs, print runs and money. He died bankrupt in 1907.
bio_note: One hundred and eight letters; four are quoted or described here (printed 1006, 1098, 1111, 1141). Dates not recorded and none inferred. The correspondence is not purely business - 'I miss you very much' (printed ~1101), 'It was a great delight seeing you' (printed 1025), 'my life here is too lonely. I wish you would' (printed 1141).
